Synopsis:
    The Indian rupee hit a two-month high driven by $136.4bn in fresh inflows, boosting RBI FX reserves to a record $729.3bn. While this strengthens India's capacity to absorb external shocks, the RBI's forward book is also at an all-time high ($137bn), capping rupee upside. Key near-term headwinds include rising crude oil prices (Brent +7% w/w) on renewed US-Iran tensions, a widening trade deficit risk, and a stronger dollar supported by elevated Fed rate hike expectations (2-in-3 odds for this month). India's BoP is projected to swing to a ~$66bn surplus this fiscal year.
